summary: Ernst Sittig was a linguist who studied at the University of Jena, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (Ph.D.) under Friedrich Bechtel. He held professorships at the University of Königsberg and the University of Tübingen.

Ernst Steinkellner is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna. He served as Director at the University of Vienna and at the Austrian Academy of Sciences' Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Ernst Trumpp was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Tübinger Stift and the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and Heinrich Ewald. He held posts at East India House, the University of Tübingen, and the University of Munich.

Ernst Waldschmidt was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kiel University and the Humboldt University of Berlin under Emil Sieg and Heinrich Lüders, later serving at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin.

Ernst Wilhelm von Brücke studied at Heidelberg University and the Humboldt University of Berlin (Dr.med.). He was a professor of physiology at the University of Königsberg (1848) and the University of Vienna (1849–1890).

Ernst Windisch was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of Leipzig under Georg Curtius, Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, Friedrich Zarncke, and Hermann Brockhaus. He held chairs at the universities of Heidelberg, Strasbourg, and Leipzig.
Ernst Zinn worked in linguistics and related fields. He held academic posts at the University of Hamburg (~1947–1951), Saarland University (1951–1956), and the University of Tübingen (~1951–1975).
Ernst Zupitza was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. from the Humboldt University of Berlin. From 1901 to 1917, he served as Privatdozent at the University of Greifswald, succeeding Heinrich Zimmer.

Ernő Hetényi worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying as a disciple under Anagarika Govinda (~1952–1985). He founded the Magyarországi Buddhista Misszió in 1951 and the Kőrösi Csoma Sándor Buddhológiai Intézet in 1956.

Ervin Baktay was an Indologist and art historian who studied at the Hungarian University of Fine Arts. He served as Curator of the Indian Section at the Ferenc Hopp Museum of Asiatic Arts (1946–1958) and lectured at SOAS in 1962.
Erwin Alexis Schwanbeck was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Bonn in 1840 and at the University of Greifswald from circa 1840 to 1844.

Erwin Panofsky was an art historian who studied at Berlin, Munich, and Freiburg under Walter Friedländer. He held positions at the University of Hamburg, New York University, Harvard University, Princeton University, and the Institute for Advanced Study.
Erwin Rohde was a classical and religious studies scholar who studied at Bonn and Leipzig. He held posts at the universities of Kiel, Jena, Tübingen, Leipzig, and Heidelberg between 1872 and 1898.

Erwin Rousselle was a sinologist and Buddhologist who studied at Munich, Freiburg, Berlin, Heidelberg, and TU Darmstadt. He held posts at Peking University, Yenching University, Tsinghua University, TU Darmstadt, Goethe University Frankfurt, and the China-Institut Frankfurt.
Esben Andreasen, a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, studied at the University of Copenhagen and was a visiting researcher at Otani University in 1992.
Esha Meher is a scholar of Indology and linguistics affiliated with Yale University, where she is attested as a graduate student.

Eshin Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Zenkei Shibayama and earned a Ph.D. from Kyoto University. He served as director at Hanazono University and head of the Institute for Zen Studies.
Esho Kawasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as director of the Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 1999) and president of Kyushu Ryukoku Gakkai (attested 2002).
Esho Mikogami was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University until 2003 and was president of the Ryukoku Buddhist Society in 1997.

Esho Sasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held posts as an assistant professor at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and as a professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).
